quickSummary: Curated analysis of 10 high-yield NEST/INBO exam traps covering interkinesis vs interphase replication, ploidy vs DNA content doubling, centromere behavior in Anaphase I vs II, crossing over partners, and cytokinesis directions.
summary: Curated analysis of 10 high-yield NEST/INBO exam traps covering interkinesis vs interphase replication, ploidy vs DNA content doubling, centromere behavior in Anaphase I vs II, crossing over partners, and cytokinesis directions.
commonMistakes: Believing DNA replication occurs during both Interphase and Interkinesis (DNA replication occurs STRICTLY during S-Phase of Interphase; Interkinesis lacks an S-phase entirely).
Thinking chromosome number doubles during S-phase when DNA doubles (Chromosome number remains CONSTANT at 2n during S-phase; only DNA content doubles from 2C to 4C).
Assuming centromeres split during Anaphase I of Meiosis I (Centromeres DO NOT split during Anaphase I; homologous chromosomes separate, and centromeres split in Anaphase II).
Thinking crossing over occurs between sister chromatids of the same chromosome (Crossing over occurs between NON-SISTER chromatids of homologous chromosomes).
Believing plant cell cytokinesis occurs centripetally via a cleavage furrow (Plant cytokinesis occurs CENTRIFUGALLY inside to outside via a Cell Plate along the phragmoplast).
Thinking chiasmata become visible during Zygotene when synapsis begins (Chiasmata become visible during DIPLOTENE upon dissolution of the Synaptonemal Complex).
Assuming the nuclear envelope disintegrates during early Prophase (Nuclear envelope breakdown is completed at late Prophase / Prometaphase).
Believing bivalents align on a single metaphase plate in Meiosis I (Bivalents align on a DOUBLE metaphase plate in Metaphase I).
Thinking cells in G0 phase are dead or metabolically dormant (Cells in G0 are metabolically active and differentiated, having exited the proliferative cycle).
Assuming human female oocytes complete Meiosis I during embryonic development (Female primary oocytes arrest in Diplotene/Dictyotene stage of Prophase I during fetal life and resume at ovulation).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Centromeres do NOT split in Anaphase I. Crossing over is between NON-SISTER chromatids. Plant cytokinesis is CENTRIFUGAL.

conceptBreakdown.content:
| Misconception / Trap | Biological Reality | Exam Tip / Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *"DNA replication occurs during both Interphase and Interkinesis."* | DNA replication occurs **STRICTLY during S-Phase of Interphase**. Interkinesis lacks an S-phase entirely. | Interkinesis is the brief phase between Meiosis I & II. |
| *"Chromosome number doubles during S-phase when DNA doubles."* | Chromosome number remains **CONSTANT ($2n$) during S-phase**; only the DNA content doubles ($2C \rightarrow 4C$). | Sister chromatids remain joined at centromeres. |
| *"Centromeres split during Anaphase I of Meiosis I."* | Centromeres **DO NOT split during Anaphase I**. Homologous chromosomes separate; centromeres split in Anaphase II. | Anaphase I separates homologs; Anaphase II separates sister chromatids. |
| *"Crossing over occurs between sister chromatids of the same chromosome."* | Crossing over occurs **between NON-SISTER chromatids of homologous chromosomes**. | Mediated by recombinase enzymes at pachytene. |
| *"Plant cell cytokinesis occurs centripetally via a cleavage furrow."* | Plant cytokinesis occurs **CENTRIFUGALLY (inside to outside) via a Cell Plate (Phragmoplast)**. | Animal cytokinesis is centripetal (outside to inside). |
| *"Chiasmata become visible during Zygotene when synapsis begins."* | Chiasmata become visible during **DIPLOTENE** upon dissolution of the Synaptonemal Complex. | Synapsis occurs at Zygotene; crossing over at Pachytene. |
| *"The nuclear envelope disintegrates during early Prophase."* | Nuclear envelope breakdown is completed at **late Prophase / Prometaphase**. | Reassembles during Telophase. |
| *"Bivalents align on a single metaphase plate in Meiosis I."* | Bivalents align on a **DOUBLE metaphase plate in Metaphase I**. Single plates form in Mitosis and Metaphase II. | Double plates allow homolog disjunction in Anaphase I. |
| *"Cells in G₀ phase are dead or metabolically dormant."* | Cells in $G_0$ are **metabolically active and differentiated**, but have exited the cell proliferation cycle. | Neurons and cardiac cells reside permanently in $G_0$. |
| *"Human female oocytes complete Meiosis I during embryonic development."* | Female primary oocytes arrest in **Diplotene (Dictyotene stage) of Prophase I** during fetal life and resume at ovulation. | Arrest can persist for $12\text{--}50\text{ years}$. |
